title: Riemann Sums
short: A sum of f(xᵢ)Δx approximates the area; more rectangles do better.

blocks.html: Left and right sums are two choices among many. We may sample each strip anywhere: at the midpoint, at the highest point, at the lowest point. All such sums are called Riemann sums, and as the strips get thinner they all approach the same number.

A Riemann sum for $f$ on $[a, b]$ is $\displaystyle\sum_{\role{index}{i}=1}^{n} \role[height of strip i]{output}{f(x_i^*)}\,\role[strip width]{input}{\Delta x}$, where $x_i^*$ is any sample point in the $i$th strip. The midpoint sum $M_n$ uses the middle of each strip. For a continuous $f$, every choice of sample points gives the same limit as $n \to \infty$.

blocks.name: riemann

opts.task: Increase $n$ and compare the four methods in the table. The midpoint sum is usually the closest.

blocks.cap: Riemann sums for $x^2$ on $[0, 2]$. All of them close in on $\frac{8}{3}$ as $n$ grows.

blocks.html: For a continuous function on a thin strip, the highest and lowest values are close together, so every sample point gives nearly the same height. The upper sum (highest points) and lower sum (lowest points) trap every other Riemann sum between them, and their difference shrinks to 0 as the strips narrow. So all the sums share one limit. The midpoint often does best because, on a strip where the curve is nearly straight, its overshoot on one half cancels its undershoot on the other.

blocks.title: A sum in sigma notation
blocks.q: Evaluate $\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{4}\left(1 + \frac{i}{2}\right)^{2}\cdot\frac{1}{2}$, and name the integral it approximates.
steps: It is a right sum with $\Delta x = \frac{1}{2}$ for $f(x) = x^2$, starting at $a = 1$ (sample points $1.5, 2, 2.5, 3$), so $b = 3$.
blocks.a: $10.75$, an estimate of the area under $x^2$ from 1 to 3 (exactly $\frac{26}{3} \approx 8.67$; the right sum overshoots).

blocks.title: Taking the limit
blocks.q: For $f(x) = x$ on $[0, 1]$, the right sum is $R_n = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\frac{i}{n}$. Find $\lim_{n \to \infty} R_n$.
blocks.a: $\frac{1}{2}$, the area of the triangle under $y = x$, exactly as geometry says.

blocks.html: Using the left or right endpoints when the midpoint was asked, or using midpoints of the wrong strips. The midpoint of $[x_{i-1}, x_i]$ is $x_{i-1} + \frac{\Delta x}{2}$. Check: the first midpoint should be half a strip to the right of $a$.
